scenes.question: What technology do the local Dispatcher Tools use to run the Dispatcher?
scenes.heading: Docker
scenes.body: The local Dispatcher Tools are Docker-based. They run an Apache HTTP Server with the AEM Dispatcher module inside a Docker container, providing the same caching and filtering behavior as the cloud Dispatcher.

scenes.question: What script do you use to start the local Dispatcher with hot-reload enabled?
scenes.heading: ./bin/docker_run_hot_reload.sh
scenes.body: The local Dispatcher is started with `./bin/docker_run_hot_reload.sh ./src localhost:4503 8080`. The hot-reload variant is preferred because it automatically reloads Dispatcher configuration when files change.

scenes.question: On which port does the local Dispatcher expose the site when using the standard startup command?
scenes.heading: Port 8080
scenes.body: The startup command `./bin/docker_run_hot_reload.sh ./src localhost:4503 8080` exposes the local Dispatcher on port 8080. This is where you access the site as it would appear through the Dispatcher (cached, filtered requests).

scenes.question: Which local Publish port does the Dispatcher connect to in the standard startup command?
scenes.heading: localhost:4503
scenes.body: In the command `./bin/docker_run_hot_reload.sh ./src localhost:4503 8080`, `localhost:4503` is the address of the local Publish instance. The Dispatcher proxies requests from port 8080 to Publish at 4503.

scenes.question: What is the advantage of using docker_run_hot_reload.sh over docker_run.sh?
scenes.heading: It reloads Dispatcher configuration automatically when files change
scenes.body: The `docker_run_hot_reload.sh` script monitors the Dispatcher configuration directory and reloads the configuration automatically when files change. This avoids needing to restart the Docker container during development.

scenes.question: What tool do you use to validate local Dispatcher configuration before deploying?
scenes.heading: ./bin/validate ./src
scenes.body: The command `./bin/validate ./src` checks your Apache and Dispatcher configuration for errors before deploying. It helps catch configuration mistakes locally, before they reach Cloud Manager.
